summary: The milestone completed 14 experiments in 3.4 minutes, including 10 compute-bound experiments. The authenticated GGUF receipt task and two receipt-gated tasks formed the measured execution tail, but the records do not establish a compute-task GPU-idle fault.
bottlenecks_identified: Execution time was concentrated in the authenticated GGUF receipt task and two receipt-gated tasks. Why those tasks were longest: no data available this milestone.
Timing came from disk-mtime reconstruction because the live git-log path found no commits. This limits causal analysis of short tasks.

The GPU report is a point-in-time snapshot rather than task-linked telemetry. It cannot grade GPU efficiency during compute execution. No data available this milestone shows that a compute-bound task loaded two or more models in parallel, so no missed DualGPURunner dispatch can be established.
improvements_suggested: Record monotonic start and stop times for each experiment phase so the next retrospective does not depend on disk modification times.
Attach GPU utilization samples to each compute-bound task and mark synthesis-only intervals explicitly.

Record requested model count, parallel intent, selected runner, and GPU assignment in each execution receipt. Select DualGPURunner automatically only when two or more models are requested in parallel.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add experiment-scoped phase timers to the conductor artifact.
Add task-scoped GPU sampling for compute-bound execution.
Add model-concurrency and runner-selection receipts, with conditional DualGPURunner dispatch for parallel multi-model work.
meta_reflection: The supplied data supports a runtime ranking, but it does not support a causal explanation, a task-period GPU efficiency grade, or a parallel-runner finding. The next milestone should store timing, GPU samples, model concurrency, and runner selection in one task receipt.
